body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}-\widehat M_{it})+\widehat B_2,\quad (\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\)

sampling_model.design: A deterministic common-start treatment block \(G\times W\) removes untreated potential outcomes from the completion sample; inference is conditional on the mask and the low-rank signal.
sampling_model.units: Conditional on the signal, row laws factor across units. Within each row the centered process has common stationary covariance, fixed known dependence range \(q\), and a uniform conditional sub-Gaussian exponential-moment bound.
sampling_model.treatment: Treated outcomes \(Y_{it}(1)\) are observed on \(G\times W\); their counterfactual mean component \(M_{it}\) is imputed from donor and pretreatment observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Donor and pretreatment factor Grams have explicit normalized eigenvalue bounds, and every target restriction retains a fixed positive fraction of the global signal. The proved proportional-cohort theorem assumes the sufficient local envelope \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\), which is \(\omega_n n^{3/4}\ell_n^2\) when \(H\asymp n\) and \(\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^3\) when \(H\) is fixed. Its score variance is of order \((nH)^{-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known rank is used in the native local nuclear-norm and rank-projection fits. Every target-specific native and auxiliary fit uses the same ordered \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\) chart and restriction map \(R_{it}\). A target-specific auxiliary fit measurable with respect to \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\) supports leave-neighborhood conditioning. Pretreatment residuals estimate finite-lag covariance, while fitted tangent weights and fitted projector Hessians estimate variance and serial curvature.
sampling_model.randomness: All probability statements are with respect to the rowwise error processes, conditional on \(M\), \(A\), and the realized treated potential outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v), subgroup nuclear-norm completion permits one-date inference for imputed entries with independent cell noise and its stated subgroup-size and loading regimes.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The published-reduction proposition only on the explicit class intersection; the feasible-window theorem adds serial dependence and growing windows under this note's strengthened uniform class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Leave-neighbor-out analysis gives weak-factor principal-component normality under dependent noise in a fully observed matrix.
Auxiliary leave-one-out estimators are asymptotically equivalent to the feasible nuclear-norm-based estimator without sample splitting.
Residual HAC estimators consistently estimate covariance matrices for weak-factor tensor loading scores with missing observations.
Convex and nonconvex matrix-completion solutions are tightly coupled under independent random entry sampling.
Double-debiased matrix completion yields confidence intervals for general linear forms under random entry sampling.
Residual block bootstrap confidence intervals cover fixed-cell treatment effects under weakly dependent factor errors.
Adjusted principal components provide pointwise factor and loading inference with general missing observations and dependent errors.
Factor and loading limit distributions are derived under general missing-data patterns.
Bias-aware confidence intervals attain uniformly correct coverage over weak interactive effects for admissible regressors.
Analytically bias-corrected alternating maximization is asymptotically normal for regression coefficients under unbalanced interactive effects.

body.tldr: For a deterministic common-start missing block, the native one-missing-cell convex optimizer has a complete three-block tangent score and a serial rank-projection drift. Neighborhood replacement through the native fixed point, centered quadratic aggregation, residual finite-lag covariance estimation, and fitted Hessian and weight stability yield feasible uniform scalar Wald inference whenever \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\) with \(\omega_n\to\infty\). This is a sufficient envelope, not a sharp frontier.

project_justification.gap: Choi and Yuan's deterministic-MNAR result treats independent cell noise under its own subgroup-size, loading, and rate conditions, while dependent-noise factor and residual-HAC results do not control the implemented masked convex completion estimator at the shrinking standard-error scale of a growing causal window. The Choi--Yuan class and this note's strengthened uniform class are not nested.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a native-optimizer second-order expansion whose first differential retains donor-window, treated-pre, and negative donor-pre overlap terms and whose projector curvature is contracted against finite-lag covariance, with all errors controlled at the oracle window scale.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies that expansion, a feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction, an influence-weighted residual covariance estimator, an independent-row finite-range central limit theorem, and uniform Wald coverage under the rate-exact sufficient envelope \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\). The one-date Choi--Yuan reduction is stated only on the explicit intersection with their Conditions (i)--(v), while the separate exponent-indexed sharp-frontier question remains open.

body.related_work: Choi and Yuan (2024) provide the deterministic-MNAR subgroup nuclear-norm and rank-projection architecture under independent cell noise and their stated subgroup-size, loading, and rate conditions. This note is an extension of their balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class; neither full class contains the other, and the formal one-date reduction is only on the explicit intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v). Choi and Yuan (2025) provide the fully observed leave-neighbor weak-factor precedent; the present proof transfers neighborhood replacement through the actual masked convex fixed point. Cen and Lam (2025) motivate residual HAC for missing-factor scores, whereas the present result contracts fitted rank-projection Hessians and aggregate influence weights against finite-lag covariance. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) supply only a backup coupling pattern and do not replace the estimator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Uniformity requires exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, balanced dimensions, a proportional treated cohort, normalized donor and pretreatment Gram bounds, local-to-global signal comparability, conditional sub-Gaussian tails, and \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\). The proof uses a one-missing-coordinate common-start chart and fixed-range dependency-graph coloring. It does not establish larger missing local blocks, unknown rank, heterogeneous or long-range covariance, simultaneous event-time bands, or validity at the proportional-window spectral-noise boundary; the sufficient envelope is not claimed sharp.
body.honest_scope: The proved class conditions on exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, conditionally independent rows, genuine within-row finite-range dependence, common stationary covariance, conditional sub-Gaussian tails, a fixed positive local-to-global signal ratio, a proportional treated cohort, bounded aspect ratios, and explicit donor and pretreatment restricted-Gram bounds. It covers growing windows under \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\), including \(H\asymp n\) at sufficient order \(\omega_n n^{3/4}\ell_n^2\) and the rank-one calibration \(\psi=n^{4/5}\). It does not claim that this is the sharp frontier, that its class contains the full Choi--Yuan class, or that \(q=0,H=1\) makes the classes identical. It does not cover simultaneous event-time bands, unknown rank, heterogeneous covariance, hidden-block identification, rank overprojection, or proportional-window inference arbitrarily close to signal order \(n^{1/2}\).
body.interpretation: The confidence interval concerns one scalar: the realized treated cohort's average sustained effect over the declared consecutive post window. For the SEC Tick Size Pilot reanalysis, it supports a cohort-window liquidity contrast after native completion and serial-curvature correction; it is not an event-time band.
